title: Adaptive slot shrinking with predictive KV working-set forecasting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Continuous batching on shared GPU pools can lead to long-tail latency spikes when tenants have unexpectedly large KV working sets. Current preemption strategies are binary (preempt or not) and evict whole entries, which causes throughput regressions or noisy neighbor effects. We need a smoother, predictive approach that shrinks a tenant's active slot footprint progressively while forecasting KV resonance so we hit latency SLOs without heavy tail preemption.
goals: Reduce 95th and 99th percentile latency violations under mixed workloads by 30% compared to baseline preemption
Lower unnecessary KV evictions (measured as re-population rate) by 25%
Introduce an orthogonal, low-overhead forecasting signal to guide slot shrinking decisions that integrates with the scheduler and KV manager
acceptance_criteria: New scheduler exposes 'slot_shrink_score' per tenant that maps to a continuous throttle (0.0-1.0)
Under synthetic mixed workloads (short-chat-heavy + long-context-heavy tenants) P95 latency decreases by >=25% vs current preemptor with equivalent throughput
KV re-population rate (reinsertions/evictions) drops by >=20% on long-session tenants
No regression in median latency or overall throughput beyond 5%
Feature gated and can be A/B rolled per-tenant via Console rollout policies
implementation_notes: 1) Add lightweight online predictor that maintains exponential-weighted history of per-tenant KV footprint growth rate and probability of high-residency events over next 30s.
2) Compute 'forecasted_resonance' = alpha * recent_growth + beta * burst_score + gamma * slot_pressure where coefficients are tunable via runtime flags.
3) Map forecasted_resonance to 'shrink_ratio' (0..0.5) which instructs the batcher to reduce target slot allocation for that tenant gradually instead of immediate preemption.
4) When shrink ratio applied, KV manager marks low-reuse entries for soft-eviction (LRU-backed aging) but retains a small hotset pinned for immediate reuse to avoid re-population storms.
5) Integrate telemetry hooks: per-tenant shrink_ratio, forecast input features, evictions marked soft vs hard, and downstream latency before/after shrink events.
6) Implement canary with 10% of traffic on Dedicated clusters and a controlled load generator for mixed workload validation.
design_decisions: Prefer gradual slot shrinking over immediate tenant preemption to smooth latency impact and reduce cold-cache penalties.
Forecast horizon chosen as 30s to balance recency vs stability; we observed most working-set bursts resolve within 10-40s in replay traces.
Soft-eviction (age-based) chosen to reduce reinsert storms; hard evictions reserved for severe memory pressure or emergency reclaim.
Keep forecasting model intentionally simple (EWMA + heuristic burst detector) to avoid heavy compute on hot code path and ease explainability for SRE/Customer support.
risks: Forecasting false positives could shrink slots unnecessarily and harm throughput for bursty but short-lived tenants.
If soft-evictions are tuned too leniently, GPU memory pressure may escalate and trigger emergency hard evictions.
Complex interactions with existing quota-based fairers and credit accounting—risk of double-counting shrink effects leading to unfair tenant outcomes.
Monitoring gaps: insufficient telemetry could make it hard to pinpoint whether regressions are from forecasting or from batcher scheduling changes.
mitigations: Start with conservative shrink caps (max 20% slot reduction in initial canary) and raise after observing safety metrics.
Add a safety circuit that converts shrink instructions to immediate hard preemption only if GPU free memory < 5% and latency SLOs are critically violated.
Coordinate with quota accounting owners to expose a single reconciliation point that consumes shrink_ratio as an input rather than modifying two independent systems.
Ship detailed dashboard tiles (Console) for early detection: per-tenant forecast_confidence, shrink_ratio over time, soft-eviction counts, re-population rate.
notes_for_qa: Create mixed-workload harness with: 60% short-turnaround chat sessions (<=64 tokens), 30% long-context sessions (>=2k tokens), 10% embedding/backfill traffic.
Assertions: steady-state memory usage, soft-eviction count, re-population rate, P95/P99 latency per tenant, CPU overhead of predictor <2%.
Failure injection: simulate sudden KV working-set doubling for a tenant and validate shrink triggers without triggering global OOM.
plan_timeline: Week 1: implement predictor, telemetry events, basic shrink_ratio plumbing (local tests)
Week 2: integrate with batcher + KV manager, run unit/integration tests
Week 3: internal perf-run on staging clusters, tune coefficients and soft-eviction thresholds
Week 4: canary rollout to 10% Dedicated traffic, monitor metrics and iterate
Week 5: expand rollout to 50% and prepare runtime-1.20 release notes
